title: Monologue: The Agent Talks to Itself While It Listens | Waterr Research
excerpt: A research preview of Monologue — the reasoning harness inside Waterr's AI meetings. A slot-typed sidecar lets a realtime voice model think while the user speaks: +25% relative on Scale AI's AudioMC, no added turn latency.
content_html:
Human conversation is bidirectional and real-time. Between our turns, we think, and that thinking is what keeps a long conversation coherent, what surfaces real value, what lets us hold a thread across the whole hour. State-of-the-art real-time voice models don't do this. They may carry frontier-level intelligence, but the moment you put them into a long, high-stakes conversation they bottleneck: no room to reason between turns, no memory of a rule set six turns ago, no coherent thread across half an hour. Today we're publishing our first research note on the architecture that closes that gap: Monologue (the architecture our whitepaper calls ORI, the Omni-model Reasoning Infrastructure). Monologue lets a real-time voice model think in chunks while the user is still speaking, so its next move is deliberate and informed by everything that came before, without skyrocketing the per-minute price to a level nobody can afford in production.

The result, measured on a public benchmark: Thinking-tier conversation quality at Instant-tier latency, at roughly a third of the cost of the nearest Thinking-tier system – on the same frozen backbone. It ships as an API at a flat $0.03 per conversation-minute, planner included. The model that speaks should not have to be the model that thinks.

The failure everyone who has talked to a voice AI has met

Thirty minutes into a screening interview, the candidate said it in minute four: "I can't relocate before March." In minute thirty-one, a bare real-time voice model cheerfully proposes a February start date on-site. The candidate notices. The meeting is over in every way that matters, even though it keeps going.

That moment – the forgotten fact, the contradicted commitment, the dropped instruction, the ignored correction – is the signature failure of real-time voice AI, and it is catalogued systematically by Audio MultiChallenge (Scale AI, 2025). It is not four separate bugs. It is one failure: information routing under a latency constraint. Real-time voice models – Google's gemini-live-2.5-flash-native-audio, OpenAI's gpt-realtime-2, Thinking Machines' interaction-small – live inside a ~200–500 ms turn-taking window that forecloses the extended chain-of-thought budgets text-mode reasoning models routinely use. Even where a thinking_config is exposed on paper, the current generation of production speech-to-speech SKUs typically rejects it at request time.

The model has enough capacity. It does not have the right context at the right moment. Our ablation shows this directly: an oracle planner that sees the literal upcoming user turn lifts factual recall by +24.1 points on the same frozen backbone. The bottleneck is not the model. It is what reaches the model, and when.

The engineering question is therefore not how to make the voice model reason harder in-band – that breaks the pacing that makes a conversation feel human, and multiplies the per-minute cost. It is where the informing deliberation lives. (Decision researchers have a name for this shape: fast expert decisions are good because the deliberate work already happened, somewhere else, in advance.) Prompt engineering pre-loads context statically and cannot adapt as the conversation moves. Long-term memory gives the fast path a bigger buffer but does no fresh reasoning over it. In-band reasoning makes the user wait.

For voice AI to reason at frontier quality without breaking conversational latency, deliberation must live off the critical path.

Our approach

The interface: an AI that is in the meeting with you

Waterr's product surface is what we call an omni-model interface: you are present in a video call with the AI, and the AI participates through audio. Video-in captures your face, environment, and screen; audio-out returns natural speech. No lip-sync, no talking-head avatar, no synthetic reciprocity. (The name describes the product surface; the evaluation in this note covers the audio reasoning path.)

This asymmetry is deliberate. In production observation, users tired of synthetic reciprocity quickly; they wanted a productive collaborator that speaks, not a synthetic interlocutor to perform reciprocity toward. The user is a face plus a voice plus a room; the AI is a voice plus a reasoning process. That is a feature, not an omission – and it means the interface pushes far more context in per unit time than a voice-only agent, which makes the sidecar's job both more valuable (there is more to reason over) and more tractable (higher-fidelity signal to reason from). The lineage is the omni-model line from Alibaba's Qwen team – Qwen2.5-Omni (Qwen Team, 2025) – adopted at the harness level rather than inside a single model: the sidecar can call the vision, retrieval, and tool capabilities of whichever reasoning model it runs, on top of a frozen audio backbone.

Monologue is the mechanism that turns that dense multimodal input into cross-turn coherence at conversational speed. It has been the deep-think processor inside Waterr's production meeting engine since June.

The reasoning sidecar: thinking between the turns

Our starting point is a frozen speech-to-speech backbone (gemini-live-2.5-flash-native-audio) that cannot reason in-band. Several design choices make Monologue work.

Off-band reasoning, not in-band. The sidecar is a separate text-side model that observes the transcript, produces a briefing, and injects it into the voice model's session in the audio gap that already exists between turns – before the next audio streams in. Wall time is unchanged; the user hears no pause.

Slot-typed thoughts, not free-form summarisation. Our first sidecar emitted three unstructured analytical bullets. It was null on factual recall (−0.4 pts on the benchmark's memory axis) – the voice model treated free-form bullets as background chatter. The failure was not summarisation; it was the carrier shape. Monologue instead uses a slot-typed contract: MEMORY (verbatim user-stated facts – quoted, not paraphrased), CONSTRAINT (the bot's own prior commitments plus an enforcement clause), TRAJECTORY (the prescriptive action for the next reply). Each slot is one full sentence; a runtime parser stitches them into a flowing background paragraph the model reads before it speaks. In the vignette above, the MEMORY slot is carrying "user said: 'I can't relocate before March'" into the model's context at minute thirty-one. Under this contract the sidecar recovers +7 to +16 pts on factual recall (depending on baseline run) – a substantial fraction of the oracle-context gap – without any leak of the upcoming user turn.

Injection format is a first-class variable. Injecting content between turns risks the model treating it as a completed prior turn and going silent – we hit exactly this with a 23% empty-reply rate on our first slot-typed planner. Joining the slots into one paragraph and softening the wrapper to [Background note – read silently before you speak your reply. Do not read this aloud.] dropped the empty rate to 3.2%. Silent-injection stability is something we measure on every backend we support.

Mid-turn injection: think while they're still speaking. The sidecar doesn't have to wait for the user to finish. A parallel STT transcript feeds a debouncer that inspects each partial as it arrives and releases the planner only when four gates all pass – the transcript has stayed stable for ≥ 0.6 s, is at least 20 characters long, has grown by 25 characters since the last firing, and 2.5 s have passed since the last firing. On a long user turn the planner can fire two or three times before the user is done, and each slot update is injected silently into the live session – so the model already has the latest reasoning loaded when it opens its reply. Currently supported on Gemini Live only (needs the parallel STT stream); all four gates are per-deployment tunable.

A zero-leak protocol. The sidecar sees turns 1..K−1 only, never the upcoming user turn. This is what makes the number reproducible in production, where the sidecar cannot see the future. The oracle condition (which does see turn K) is reserved as a diagnostic ceiling.

Backbone-agnostic by construction. The sidecar is a contract, not a model: any reasoning model can fill it (Claude Sonnet 5 does, in this preview, at ≈$0.004 per call), and any voice backbone that exposes a mid-session injection primitive can receive it. This is the strategic property of the design: every frontier-model improvement, from any vendor, makes Waterr meetings better the week it ships – we pick the best backbone and the best planner per deployment, and re-pick when the frontier moves. Vendors will ship thinking-capable voice models natively; Monologue wraps those too. A vendor optimises a model. We optimise the meeting.

What it does in a meeting

  • Remembers what was said. Verbatim facts from early turns – names, numbers, constraints – reach the model at the moment they're needed (MEMORY).
  • Keeps its own commitments. The model is reminded of what it already promised, with an enforcement clause (CONSTRAINT).
  • Follows the brief. The next reply's concrete action – the rule being applied, the edit being made – is named before the model speaks (TRAJECTORY).
  • Knows where it is in the meeting. Opening, middle, closing, final-minutes: a closing question is answered differently than an opening one.
  • Dials thinking depth per deployment. The sidecar can call any reasoning model on the price/quality curve; the backbone stays fast.
  • Adds no conversation wall time. 22.5 s bare vs 22.5 s with the sidecar per benchmark conversation – the sidecar is structurally off the latency path.
  • Stays out of the transcript. Briefings are read silently; empty-reply rate in evaluation is 3.2% (5/154 conversations).

The evidence

The setup

We evaluate on Audio MultiChallenge (Scale AI, 2025) – multi-turn conversations balanced across four failure axes, judged per-rubric by an LLM judge, with the bare backbone re-run three independent times so every effect is measured against the benchmark's own run-to-run noise.

Results

Monologue lifts the same frozen backbone from 38.50% to 69.8% aggregate APR at n=140, paired against three independent baseline runs. That is +1.8 pts above the text-mode Sonnet-5 reasoning ceiling measured on the same 90 paired conversations – three of the four AudioMC axes meet or exceed that ceiling, and factual recall (INFERENCE_MEMORY) beats it by +17.6 pts (a slot-typed verbatim carrier over an audio-native backbone outperforms a frontier text reasoner reading the transcript). Planner p90 is 3.5 s, empty-transcript rate 0 of 139. In cross-vendor terms: that is Thinking-tier quality reached at Instant-tier latency, from an Instant-tier backbone.

Pricing, cost, and latency

Pricing. The Monologue API is a flat $0.03 per conversation-minute, planner included – roughly 60% below gpt-realtime-2 at xHigh (~$0.08/min), the only system in its quality territory. Flat-rate means no token metering, and every backbone improvement we adopt is priced in, not passed on.

Underlying cost. End-to-end unit cost, including planner tokens at production turn rates, is $0.03–0.05 per meeting-minute (raw audio is ≈$0.012/min at list prices; the planner adds ≈$0.004 per call at 3–4 calls per minute; prompt and history overhead make up the rest). That is roughly half of gpt-realtime-2 at xHigh reasoning (~$0.08/min at moderate token consumption).

Latency. 22.5 s (bare) vs 22.5 s (Monologue) end-to-end wall time per conversation. The sidecar runs in a gap that already exists.

What this doesn't show yet

We hold ourselves to the evidence, so three honest edges, stated plainly (the full limitations analysis is in the research paper):

  • The routing is measured at its ceiling. In this evaluation the sidecar's axis-aware routing uses the benchmark's axis labels as hints; a production planner would self-classify from conversation history. Re-running with self-classified routing is the immediate next step.
  • The headline run's judge shares a vendor with the planner. A cross-vendor agreement check on earlier-iteration records was strong (κ = 0.89 on genuinely double-judged rubrics); re-judging this run's sample with a second vendor is queued and gates any harder magnitude claim.
  • Point estimates are directional, not decimal-place claims. n=124 paired conversations; per-axis cells are small, which is why we publish the spread across three baselines rather than a single flattering column.

The road ahead, ordered by expected value: self-classified axis routing; a confirmation run on a fresh sample; cross-vendor re-judge; a retrieval-augmented planner targeting the residual oracle gap on factual recall; streaming and deferred planners; scenario-adherence evaluation on Waterr's actual production surface; cross-backbone deployment on OpenAI Realtime and other Live-capable backbones.

Try it, test it, or challenge it

Monologue runs inside every Waterr AI meeting today. If you run interviews, discovery calls, or training sessions, you can experience it directly at waterr.ai. If you build voice-first products, the Monologue API is available at a flat $0.03 per conversation-minute – reach us at [email protected] for access, to test the sidecar on your own scenarios, or to have a reasoning backend evaluated on our harness. The raw JSONL, statistics code, and reproducibility pins are available on request.

This is the strategic property of the design: every frontier-model improvement, from any vendor, makes Waterr meetings better the week it ships – we pick the best backbone and the best planner per deployment, and re-pick when the frontier moves. Vendors will ship thinking-capable voice models natively; Monologue wraps those too. A vendor optimises a model. We optimise the meeting. What it does in a meeting Remembers what was said. Verbatim facts from early turns – names, numbers, constraints – reach the model at the moment they're needed (MEMORY). Keeps its own commitments. The model is reminded of what it already promised, with an enforcement clause (CONSTRAINT). Follows the brief. The next reply's concrete action – the rule being applied, the edit being made – is named before the model speaks (TRAJECTORY). Knows where it is in the meeting. Opening, middle, closing, final-minutes: a closing question is answered differently than an opening one. Dials thinking depth per deployment. The sidecar can call any reasoning model on the price/quality curve; the backbone stays fast. Adds no conversation wall time. 22.5 s bare vs 22.5 s with the sidecar per benchmark conversation – the sidecar is structurally off the latency path. Stays out of the transcript. Briefings are read silently; empty-reply rate in evaluation is 3.2% (5/154 conversations). The evidence The setup We evaluate on Audio MultiChallenge (Scale AI, 2025) – multi-turn conversations balanced across four failure axes, judged per-rubric by an LLM judge, with the bare backbone re-run three independent times so every effect is measured against the benchmark's own run-to-run noise. Results Monologue lifts the same frozen backbone from 38.50% to 69.8% aggregate APR at n=140, paired against three independent baseline runs. That is +1.8 pts above the text-mode Sonnet-5 reasoning ceiling measured on the same 90 paired conversations – three of the four AudioMC axes meet or exceed that ceiling, and factual recall (INFERENCE_MEMORY) beats it by +17.6 pts (a slot-typed verbatim carrier over an audio-native backbone outperforms a frontier text reasoner reading the transcript). Planner p90 is 3.5 s, empty-transcript rate 0 of 139. In cross-vendor terms: that is Thinking-tier quality reached at Instant-tier latency, from an Instant-tier backbone. blocks.html_en: Human conversation is bidirectional and real-time. Between our turns, we think, and that thinking is what keeps a long conversation coherent, what surfaces real value, what lets us hold a thread across the whole hour. State-of-the-art real-time voice models don't do this. They may carry frontier-level intelligence, but the moment you put them into a long, high-stakes conversation they bottleneck: no room to reason between turns, no memory of a rule set six turns ago, no coherent thread across half an hour. Today we're publishing our first research note on the architecture that closes that gap: Monologue (the architecture our whitepaper calls ORI, the Omni-model Reasoning Infrastructure). Monologue lets a real-time voice model think in chunks while the user is still speaking, so its next move is deliberate and informed by everything that came before, without skyrocketing the per-minute price to a level nobody can afford in production.

In production observation, users tired of synthetic reciprocity quickly; they wanted a productive collaborator that speaks, not a synthetic interlocutor to perform reciprocity toward. The user is a face plus a voice plus a room; the AI is a voice plus a reasoning process. blocks.html_en: Slot-typed thoughts, not free-form summarisation. Our first sidecar emitted three unstructured analytical bullets. It was null on factual recall (−0.4 pts on the benchmark's memory axis) – the voice model treated free-form bullets as background chatter. The failure was not summarisation; it was the carrier shape. Monologue instead uses a slot-typed contract: MEMORY (verbatim user-stated facts – quoted, not paraphrased), CONSTRAINT (the bot's own prior commitments plus an enforcement clause), TRAJECTORY (the prescriptive action for the next reply). Each slot is one full sentence; a runtime parser stitches them into a flowing background paragraph the model reads before it speaks. In the vignette above, the MEMORY slot is carrying "user said: 'I can't relocate before March'" into the model's context at minute thirty-one. Under this contract the sidecar recovers +7 to +16 pts on factual recall (depending on baseline run) – a substantial fraction of the oracle-context gap – without any leak of the upcoming user turn.

blocks.html_en: Mid-turn injection: think while they're still speaking. The sidecar doesn't have to wait for the user to finish. A parallel STT transcript feeds a debouncer that inspects each partial as it arrives and releases the planner only when four gates all pass – the transcript has stayed stable for ≥ 0.6 s, is at least 20 characters long, has grown by 25 characters since the last firing, and 2.5 s have passed since the last firing. On a long user turn the planner can fire two or three times before the user is done, and each slot update is injected silently into the live session – so the model already has the latest reasoning loaded when it opens its reply. Currently supported on Gemini Live only (needs the parallel STT stream); all four gates are per-deployment tunable.

blocks.html_en: Backbone-agnostic by construction. The sidecar is a contract, not a model: any reasoning model can fill it (Claude Sonnet 5 does, in this preview, at ≈$0.004 per call), and any voice backbone that exposes a mid-session injection primitive can receive it. This is the strategic property of the design: every frontier-model improvement, from any vendor, makes Waterr meetings better the week it ships – we pick the best backbone and the best planner per deployment, and re-pick when the frontier moves. Vendors will ship thinking-capable voice models natively; Monologue wraps those too. A vendor optimises a model. We optimise the meeting.

blocks.html_en: Monologue lifts the same frozen backbone from 38.50% to 69.8% aggregate APR at n=140, paired against three independent baseline runs. That is +1.8 pts above the text-mode Sonnet-5 reasoning ceiling measured on the same 90 paired conversations – three of the four AudioMC axes meet or exceed that ceiling, and factual recall (INFERENCE_MEMORY) beats it by +17.6 pts (a slot-typed verbatim carrier over an audio-native backbone outperforms a frontier text reasoner reading the transcript). content_html_zh:
人类对话是双向的、实时的。 在我们轮流进行的间隙，我们会思考，这种思考使长时间的对话保持连贯，使真正的价值浮现出来，让我们在整个小时内保持线索。 最先进的实时语音模型无法做到这一点。 它们可能具有前沿水平的智力，但当你将它们放入一场漫长、高风险的对话时，它们就会遇到瓶颈：轮流之间没有推理的空间，没有对六轮前设定的规则的记忆，半小时内没有连贯的线索。 今天，我们发布了第一份关于缩小这一差距的架构的研究报告：Monologue（我们的白皮书将该架构称为 ORI，全模型推理基础设施）。 Monologue 让实时语音模型在用户仍在说话时进行分块思考，因此它的下一步行动是经过深思熟虑的，并根据之前发生的一切进行通知，而不会将每分钟的价格飙升至无人能承担的生产水平。

结果是根据公共基准衡量的：即时层延迟下的思考层对话质量，成本约为最近的思考层系统的三分之一 - 在相同的冻结骨干上。 它以 API 的形式提供，每通话分钟 0.03 美元，包括规划器。 会说话的模型不一定是会思考的模型。

每个与语音 AI 交谈过的人都遇到过的失败

筛选面试进行了三十分钟后，候选人在第四分钟说道：“我不能在三月之前搬家。” 在第 31 分钟，一个裸露的实时语音模型高兴地在现场提出了二月的开始日期。 候选人注意到了。 会议在所有重要方面都结束了，尽管会议仍在继续。

那一刻——被遗忘的事实、矛盾的承诺、被丢弃的指令、被忽略的纠正——是实时语音人工智能的标志性失败，它被 Audio MultiChallenge (Scale AI, 2025) 系统地记录下来。 这不是四个单独的错误。 这是一种失败：延迟约束下的信息路由。 实时语音模型——谷歌的gemini-live-2.5-flash-native-audio、OpenAI的gpt-realtime-2、Thinking Machines的interaction-small——存在于大约200-500毫秒的轮流窗口内，该窗口排除了文本模式推理模型通常使用的扩展思想链预算。 即使在纸上公开 Thinking_config，当前一代的生产语音到语音 SKU 通常也会在请求时拒绝它。

该模型具有足够的容量。 它在正确的时刻没有正确的背景。 我们的消融直接表明了这一点：预言机规划器在看到即将到来的用户轮流后，在同一冻结主干上将事实召回率提高了 +24.1 点。 瓶颈不是模型。 它是到达模型的内容以及时间。

因此，工程问题不在于如何让语音模型在带内推理变得更加困难——这打破了使对话感觉更人性化的节奏，并使每分钟的成本成倍增加。 这是提供信息的深思熟虑的地方。 （决策研究人员为这种形状起了一个名字：快速的专家决策是好的，因为深思熟虑的工作已经在其他地方提前进行了。） 提示工程静态地预加载上下文，并且无法随着对话的移动而调整。 长期记忆为快速路径提供了更大的缓冲区，但没有对其进行新的推理。 带内推理使用户等待。

为了让语音人工智能在不破坏对话延迟的情况下以前沿质量进行推理，深思熟虑必须远离关键路径。

我们的方法

界面：与你会面的人工智能

Waterr 的产品界面就是我们所说的全模型界面：你与 AI 进行视频通话，AI 通过音频参与。 视频输入捕捉您的脸部、环境和屏幕；音频输出返回自然语音。 没有口型同步，没有会说话的头像，没有合成互惠。 （名称描述了产品表面；本笔记中的评估涵盖了音频推理路径。）

这种不对称是故意的。 在生产观察中，用户很快就厌倦了综合互易性；他们想要一个富有成效的会说话的合作者，而不是一个需要互惠的合成对话者。 用户是一张脸加上一个声音加上一个房间； AI是一个声音加上一个推理过程。 这是一个功能，而不是一个遗漏——这意味着该界面在单位时间内推送的上下文比纯语音代理要多得多，这使得 sidecar 的工作更有价值（有更多的推理），也更容易处理（推理的保真度更高的信号）。 该谱系是来自阿里巴巴 Qwen 团队的全模型系列 - Qwen2.5-Omni（Qwen 团队，2025） - 在线束级别而不是在单个模型中采用：sidecar 可以在冻结的音频主干之上调用其运行的任何推理模型的视觉、检索和工具功能。

独白是一种将密集的多模态输入转化为对话速度的交叉连贯性的机制。 自 6 月份以来，它一直是 Waterr 生产会议引擎内的深度思考处理器。

推理边车：在转弯之间思考

我们的起点是一个无法进行带内推理的冻结语音到语音骨干网 (gemini-live-2.5-flash-native-audio)。 多种设计选择使独白发挥作用。

带外推理，而不是带内推理。 sidecar 是一个单独的文本端模型，它观察文字记录，生成简报，并将其注入到语音模型的会话中，即在下一个音频流进入之前，轮流之间已经存在的音频间隙中。 挂墙时间不变；用户听不到停顿。

槽式思考，而非自由形式的总结。 我们的第一个边车发射了三个非结构化分析子弹。 它在事实回忆上为零（基准记忆轴上-0.4分）——语音模型将自由形式的项目符号视为背景喋喋不休。 失败不是在于总结，而是在于总结。这是载体的形状。 相反，Monologue 使用槽型合约：MEMORY（逐字用户陈述的事实 - 引用，而不是解释）、CONSTRAINT（机器人自己的先前承诺加上执行条款）、TRAJECTORY（下一个回复的规定操作）。 每个槽位都是一个完整的句子；运行时解析器将它们拼接成模型在说话之前读取的流动背景段落。 在上面的小插图中，MEMORY 槽在第 31 分钟将“用户说：‘我无法在三月之前搬迁’”传送到模型的上下文中。 根据这份合同，sidecar 在实际召回上恢复了 +7 到 +16 分（取决于基线运行）——占预言机上下文差距的很大一部分——而不会泄露即将到来的用户回合。

注入格式是一流的变量。 在回合之间注入内容可能会导致模型将其视为已完成的先前回合并陷入沉默——我们在第一个槽型规划器上以 23% 的空回复率准确地解决了这一问题。 将插槽连接成一个段落，并将包装软化为[背景注释——在说出答案之前默读。 请不要大声朗读此内容。] 空置率降至3.2%。 静默注入稳定性是我们在我们支持的每个后端上衡量的。

中途注入：在他们还在说话的时候思考。 Sidecar 不必等待用户完成。 并行 STT 转录本会向去抖器提供信息，该去抖器在每个部分到达时对其进行检查，并仅在四个门都通过时才释放规划器 - 转录本保持稳定 ≥ 0.6 秒，至少有 20 个字符长，自上次触发以来已增长 25 个字符，并且自上次触发以来已经过去了 2.5 秒。 在长时间的用户轮流中，规划器可以在用户完成之前触发两到三次，并且每个槽更新都会默默地注入到实时会话中 - 因此模型在打开其回复时已经加载了最新的推理。 目前仅在 Gemini Live 上支持（需要并行 STT 流）；所有四个门均可根据部署进行调整。

零泄漏协议。 sidecar 只看到转弯 1..K−1，而不会看到即将到来的用户转弯。 这使得该数字可以在生产中重现，而 sidecar 无法预见未来。 预言条件（确实见转 K）被保留作为诊断上限。

构造与主干网无关。 sidecar 是一个合约，而不是一个模型：任何推理模型都可以填充它（在本预览中，Claude Sonnet 5 可以填充它，每次调用约 0.004 美元），并且任何公开会话中注入原语的语音骨干都可以接收它。 这是设计的战略属性：来自任何供应商的每一项前沿模型改进，都会使 Waterr 会议在发布的那一周变得更好——我们在每次部署时选择最好的骨干和最佳规划器，并在前沿移动时重新选择。 供应商将原生提供具有思考能力的语音模型；独白也包含了这些。 供应商优化模型。 我们优化会议。

它在会议中做什么

  • 记得说过的话。 早期的逐字事实——名称、数字、约束——在需要时到达模型（记忆）。
  • 信守自己的承诺。 该模型通过强制执行条款（CONSTRAINT）提醒其已经承诺的内容。
  • 遵循简介。 下一个回复的具体操作 - 正在应用的规则，正在进行的编辑 - 在模型说话之前命名（轨迹）。
  • 知道会议的地点。 开场、中场、闭幕、最后几分钟：结束问题的回答与开场问题不同。
  • 拨动每次部署的思考深度。 sidecar可以调用价格/质量曲线上的任何推理模型；脊柱保持快速。
  • 不增加对话时间。 每个基准对话的裸机时间为 22.5 秒，而使用 sidecar 则为 22.5 秒——sidecar 在结构上脱离了延迟路径。
  • 不包含在成绩单中。 默读简报；评估中的空回复率为3.2%（5/154 次对话）。

证据

设置

我们对 Audio MultiChallenge（Scale AI，2025）进行评估——在四个失败轴上平衡的多回合对话，由法学硕士法官对每个标题进行判断，裸骨干重新运行三次独立的时间，因此每个效果都是根据基准测试本身的运行噪音来衡量的。

结果

Monologue 在 n=140 时将相同的冻结骨干从 38.50% 的总 APR 提升到 69.8%，并与三个独立的基线运行配对。 这比在相同的 90 个配对对话中测得的文本模式 Sonnet-5 推理上限高出 +1.8 分 - 四个 AudioMC 轴中的三个达到或超过了该上限，而事实回忆 (INFERENCE_MEMORY) 则超过了 +17.6 分（音频原生主干上的槽型逐字载体优于阅读转录文本的前沿文本推理器）。 Planner p90 为 3.5 s，空转录率 0 为 139。 用跨供应商的术语来说：即通过即时层骨干在即时层延迟下达到思考层质量。

定价、成本和延迟

定价。 Monologue API 的价格为每分钟对话 0.03 美元，包括规划器 – 在 xHigh 下比 gpt-realtime-2 大约低 60%（约 0.08 美元/分钟），这是其质量领域中唯一的系统。 统一费率意味着没有代币计量，我们采用的每一项骨干改进都是定价的，而不是传递的。

基础成本。 端到端单位成本（包括按生产周转率计算的规划者代币）为每分钟会议 0.03-0.05 美元（原始音频按标价计算约为 0.012 美元/分钟；规划者以每分钟 3-4 个呼叫的速度为每个呼叫增加 约 0.004 美元；提示和历史记录开销构成其余部分）。 这大约是 xHigh 推理时 gpt-realtime-2 的一半（在中等令牌消耗情况下约为 0.08 美元/分钟）。

延迟。 每次对话的端到端通话时间为 22.5 秒（裸）与 22.5 秒（独白）。 边车在已经存在的间隙中运行。

这还没有显示什么

我们坚持证据，所以三个诚实的边缘，清楚地说明（完整的局限性分析在研究论文中）：

  • 路由是在其上限处测量的。 在本次评估中，sidecar 的轴感知路由使用基准的轴标签作为提示；生产计划员会根据对话历史进行自我分类。 下一步是使用自分类路由重新运行。
  • 头条新闻的评委与策划者共享一个供应商。 对早期迭代记录的跨供应商协议检查非常强大（真正的双重判断标准上的κ = 0.89）；与第二个供应商一起重新判断本次运行的样本已排队，并阻止任何更难的幅度声明。
  • 点估计是方向性的，而不是小数点后的主张。 n=124 配对对话；每个轴的单元格都很小，这就是为什么我们发布跨三个基线而不是单个令人愉悦的列的分布。

前方道路，按期望值排序：自分类轴路由；对新鲜样品进行确认运行；跨供应商重新判断；针对事实回忆中残余预言差距的检索增强规划器；流式和延迟规划器； Waterr实际生产面的情景依从性评估； OpenAI Realtime 和其他支持 Live 的骨干网上的跨骨干网部署。
